problem: In a group of six dancers, if every possible pair dances together, what is the total number of dances?

feedback.worked_solution:
First, note that $(\frac{10}{4})$ means the same thing as ${}_{10}{C}_{4}.$

 In general, the number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

Substituting $n=10$ and $r=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{10}{C}_{4} & =\frac{10!}{(10-4)!4!} \\  & =\frac{10!}{6!4!} \\  & =\frac{10\cdot 9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot \cancel{6!}}{\cancel{6!}24} \\  & =210.\end{aligned}
$$
